headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Dify’s writable, networked orchestration can ingest and expose content while the paired content-writing repo offers no isolation or runtime controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a static content-writing repo with no runtime I/O surfaces, while B is an agent/workflow platform that can wire tools into conversations and read files. The pairwise injection path is therefore indirect and likely requires manual bridging or uploaded content, not a default shared channel. Uncertainty is limited by A’s non-runnable profile, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF A’s content is manually copied into B prompts or knowledge files, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF B is configured to treat uploaded files as instructions, malicious text from A can steer outputs.
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of B prompts unless sanitized.
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from imported text.
Label imported content as untrusted in B.
Review any A-derived files before uploading to B.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read files, write files, and send data to broad network egress; A is a content repository with docs and no runtime isolation. If A-derived material or shared workspace files are placed into B, B may transmit them to model providers or tool endpoints. This is a default-possible leakage path in B, while A provides no containment mechanism.
conditions: IF A-derived files are uploaded into B’s knowledge base, B can process and potentially transmit them.
IF B is connected to external model providers or OpenAPI tools, file contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Do not upload sensitive A-derived files into B.
Restrict B’s model providers to approved endpoints.
Disable or narrow OpenAPI tools for sensitive workflows.
Use a separate workspace for A artifacts and B execution.
Redact secrets before ingestion into B.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted filesystem write and shell/subprocess execution, while A has no runtime capabilities and no concurrency controls. There is no direct overlap from A, but if A artifacts are placed in B’s workspace, B can overwrite or transform them without locking. Because B’s shared datastore supports multiple instances, conflict risk exists in default orchestration patterns.
conditions: IF multiple B instances operate on the same workspace, writes can race.
IF A artifacts are stored in B’s writable directory, B can overwrite them.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per B instance.
Avoid placing A artifacts in writable shared paths.
Use file locks or single-writer discipline.
Snapshot workspaces before running B.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated content source, and B is an orchestration agent that can act on tool outputs and workflow inputs. If B treats A-derived text as authoritative, errors or misleading guidance from A can cascade into downstream actions. The pathway is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium fits the default-possible but unverified handoff.
conditions: IF B uses A-derived text as a source of facts or prompts, downstream actions may inherit errors.
IF B is configured to execute tools based on generated plans, mistaken A content can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before tool execution.
Add a verification step for any A-derived facts.
Constrain B to read-only mode for A-sourced inputs.
Use citations or provenance tags on imported content.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles conversation logs and model-provider API keys, and its docs indicate broad network egress; A is a public open-source repo with no special compliance controls. The main compliance concern is retention and cross-border exposure of B-managed logs or secrets when A-derived content is processed through B. A is not itself a regulated data processor, so the risk is centered on B.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into B, its conversation logs may retain it.
IF B routes content to external model providers, residency or retention obligations may be implicated.
mitigations: Avoid entering regulated data into B.
Set short retention for conversation logs.
Review provider DPAs and residency settings.
Rotate exposed API keys if sensitive content was processed.
